about: How the game uses each picture. 'textures' says which file to load and how it is cut; 'tilesets' drive the automatic ground edges; 'objects' are pieces the maps can place (rect = x, y, width, height inside the sheet; foot = tiles that block walking, relative to the tile the object stands on).

hedge.note: deepFill: (1,7) is the plain forest mass; the others have small leaves that barely touch their edges, so they can sit anywhere

canopy.about: Treetops scattered over the inside of every forest (deep 'b' tiles), so a big forest reads as leafy trees, not a flat green block. Pure decoration: forest is solid anyway. objects = art.json objects to pick from; spacing = one treetop per spacing x spacing tiles (smaller = denser).

bridge.note: Wooden_Bridge_v2: horizontal ends (0,0)/(1,0), with foam (0,1)/(1,1), middle (0,2); vertical ends (2,0)/(2,1), with foam (3,0)/(3,1), middle (2,2)

hwHedge.note: deepFill: (1,7) is the plain forest mass; the others have small leaves that barely touch their edges, so they can sit anywhere

canopy.about: Treetops scattered over the inside of every forest (deep 'b' tiles), so a big forest reads as leafy trees, not a flat green block. Pure decoration: forest is solid anyway. objects = art.json objects to pick from; spacing = one treetop per spacing x spacing tiles (smaller = denser).

characters.note: Columns: back, back-left, left, front-left, front, front-right, right, back-right. Rows: left step, standing, right step.

ui.about: Pieces of the Premium UI pack. rect = x, y, width, height inside the sheet. slice = left, right, top, bottom: the edges that keep their size when a box is stretched.

big.note: Capitals are 14 pixels tall. For titles.

small.note: Capitals are 7 pixels tall. For dialogue, labels and buttons.

iconButtons.note: Each icon has a normal frame and a pressed frame (the next number). The button art sits at x 5-27, y 4-28 inside its 32 x 32 cell.

cursors.note: Cat-paw mouse cursors, drawn twice as big so they stay crisp. Only used where there is a mouse.

creatures.about: How the wandering animals look and act. 'textures' are the colour versions (pick one with color: 0, 1, 2...). 'anims' say which row of each sheet is which animation. 'acts' are the things it does between walks. Sheets are drawn facing right; the game flips them when the animal walks left.

items.about: Everything the player can collect. 'group' decides which slot of the item bar counts it. 'tex' and 'frame' are its little picture. 'rect' (instead of 'frame') cuts the picture out of a big sheet.

chests.about: Treasure chests. 'tex' is a 5-picture sheet (closed, opening, ..., open). Each chest in a region file gives coins and maybe an item.

mailbox.about: The mailbox sheet is a grid of 32 x 48 pictures, 5 across; a frame number is row x 5 + column. Its feet are 43 pixels down its cell.

gates.about: The fence gate sheet has 16 x 16 pictures, 10 across. 'closed' is the shut gate; 'opening' are the pictures shown in order as it swings open (and back in reverse).

fishing.about: Fishing at a 'fishing' spot in a region file. 'catches' are what can bite: an item from 'items', how likely it is ('weight'), and optionally 'coins' [fewest, most] that come with it. Bobber pictures are numbers in the fishing sheet (12 across): 'idle' floats, 'dunk' is pulled under, 'splash' is the ripple.

doors.about: Doors on houses that swing open when the player comes close. 'houses' says, for each house sheet, where the door sheet's 48 x 48 picture sits: pixels from the house picture's top-left corner. The house sheet itself has an open doorway. 'opening' plays as the door opens; 'closing' plays as it shuts (a little bump at the end).

rooms.about: Rooms inside houses (world/rooms/*.json). 'void' is the colour around a room. Each style names the picture sheet and which of its 16 px pieces make the floor, the doorway and each part of the walls. A room's map is a box: 'W' walls (the top two rows are the back wall), '_' floor; its 'exit' is a '_' gap in the bottom wall. A style with "shape": "cave" draws any shape instead (Rooms.drawCave): rock with floor below shows its stone 'front', other rock its dark top; 'top' is where the 4 x 4 block of rock tops starts in the 'tex' sheet (columns: open left / both sides rock / open right / both open; rows the same for up and down); pieces are [column, row]; 'floor' pieces are mixed by place, with a 'floorRare' one every 'rareEvery' tiles or so.

ambience.about: Nature sounds (the Nature slider in Settings). 'bed' is a quiet sound that loops; 'calls' play now and then, every 'every' seconds (shortest, longest). Chosen by where the player is: a room style, else the region, else 'default'.

music.about: Background music (the Music slider in Settings). One tune for each place, chosen like the nature sounds: a room style, else the region, else 'default'. Tunes are in public/assets/music, made by scripts/tools/make-music.py. 'title' plays on the start screen. 'fade' = seconds to fade between tunes, 'loopFade' = seconds a tune's end fades into its start.
